correctness.rationale: For k<=4 odd squarefree factors, sigma(N)/N<=768/385<2. For k=5, exact comparisons force 3,5,7,q,r with q in {11,13,17,19} and bounded r<=384,64,30,25 respectively, leaving exactly 87 candidate prime pairs. Each candidate has 16 complementary divisor pairs. The attached checker certifies the absence of the target omitted-pair sum by two independent exhaustive exact algorithms for every one of these 87 cases. The six-factor witness N=937365 has exact sigma=1935360 and five omitted complementary divisor pairs summing 60630, giving 2N. Computation is exhaustive only after the demonstrated finite bound, not a sampled proof.

value.rationale: The number of distinct prime factors is a canonical arithmetic complexity parameter for the recently studied odd squarefree strongly pseudoperfect class. The theorem upgrades the preexisting six-prime example to a sharp universal structural threshold, determining the first possible support cardinality. The 87-case exact obstruction is a motivated complete classification of the last open lower support layer, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff or a restatement of known abundancy inequalities. It does not resolve the infinite primitive-family question.
